# Crossing the adoption gap · M12

Choose pilots, inspect people or edit connections on a twelve-person network. Original dense groups and the mixed ring each have 30 edges and five partners per person; hub-and-spokes has 11 edges. Link changes create a custom graph while retaining the prior layout. Click two people, drag a connection with pointer/touch, or use labelled endpoint selectors. On narrow screens the network pans horizontally. Inspection never changes pilot membership.

Placement recipes retain pilot size: concentrate in cohort A, spread across cohorts or choose highest-degree people (number order breaks ties). The same people and personal offsets remain in every network. Pinned plans freeze all assumptions; the comparison names each difference and shows current/pinned adoption at matching rounds for every person. Equal totals can hide disjoint groups. Cohort totals, partner lists and utility calculations explain individual choices.

New utility = personal benefit + coordination × [new-neighbour share + compatibility × old-neighbour share]; old utility = coordination × old-neighbour share. Isolated people receive no coordination utility. Switch only when the alternative exceeds current utility by more than friction; held pilots remain committed. Updates are simultaneous. Stable states persist when aligning comparisons; detected cycles repeat with their actual phase rather than becoming fixed outcomes. First-use columns explicitly refer to the whole simulated run.

Original group/bridge saves retain their trajectories. Local persistence, Undo, recovery/cross-tab pause and editable JSON/Markdown retain current and pinned plans, connections, inspected round and decision. Invalid imports leave work unchanged. Tests cover topology degree, equal-size placement, disjoint outcomes, independent links, isolation, cycle phase, legacy results and portable state.

Fictional deterministic coordination, complete local information and fixed preferences; no empirical calibration, persuasion, uncertainty, budget or learning. Utility is not accumulated welfare. With three identical pilots, the default dense groups reach six users while the mixed ring reaches three despite matching degree. A held hub pilot can reach everyone where a leaf pilot cannot. These are mechanism examples, not general network recommendations.
